Length-two ear paths parallel old length-two paths so old distances stay fixed. The six-block weighted circle proves the exact distance bound and every old-state witness; nonincident-cube antipodes certify each extra-state lower bound. For two extra vertices at adjacent junctions the appropriate bound is d+2<=D, not the misleading circular coordinate subtraction. Odd-girth argument uses projection of ear paths and a ring cycle. Two independent standard-library programs completed their stated exhaustive checks.

value.rationale: This is an all-size edge-deletion robustness theorem for a natural recolouring dynamics: the state count increases by six and the transition count by twelve while every old-old shortest path distance, each vertex eccentricity, and the sharp diameter remain invariant. The independent square-ear classification and parity-sensitive odd girth explain this unexpected stability and can guide analyses of perturbing graph constraints. The result is not merely a single-small-graph computation or a recolouring enumeration.
